brief.greeting: Good morning. ESP32 can now run in your browser, and you don’t need a dev board.

stories.headline: ESP32 firmware runs in-browser
stories.body: **Run chips without hardware:** Esp32sim lets you load ESP32 binaries straight into a web page, emulating the MCU entirely in JavaScript.
stories.why: You can prototype IoT code instantly, no soldering required.

stories.headline: Test LLM speed before buying hardware
stories.body: **Bench local models instantly:** Llmspeed measures inference latency on your machine, so you know if a new GPU will actually speed up your workload.
stories.why: Avoid overpaying for specs you won’t use.

stories.headline: Code search cuts token use tenfold
stories.body: **Search smarter, not harder:** XERJ indexes code, docs, logs and PDFs using 40× fewer tokens than grep and promises up to 10× lower infra costs versus ElasticSearch.
stories.why: Lower token budgets mean cheaper RAG pipelines.

highlights.title: Show HN: Esp32sim – Run ESP32 firmware in the browser
highlights.summary: Esp32sim is an open‑source ESP32 emulator that runs firmware directly in a web browser.
highlights.detail: The project compiles the ESP32 CPU core to WebAssembly, allowing developers to test code without physical hardware. A demo video shows the emulator executing typical firmware loops. The author seeks feedback on features needed for development, testing, or CI integration.

highlights.title: Show HN: Llmspeed – feel how fast a local LLM runs before you buy the hardware
highlights.summary: Llmspeed is a tool that lets users measure local LLM inference speed on their hardware before buying a new system.
highlights.detail: The service runs a quick benchmark on the user's machine, reporting latency and throughput for various model sizes. It helps avoid over‑provisioning by showing real‑world performance rather than theoretical specs. The tool is open‑source and runs on common operating systems.

highlights.title: ScrapeCreators/social-media-research-skills
highlights.summary: ScrapeCreators' GitHub repo provides AI‑driven agents for extracting social‑media data across major platforms.
highlights.detail: The toolkit integrates with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini CLI to automate tasks such as outlier detection, comment mining, and competitor analysis on TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Reddit, X, and LinkedIn. It is positioned for researchers and marketers needing scalable data collection.

highlights.title: geode-sdk/geode
highlights.summary: The geode‑sdk repository offers a C++ framework for creating Geometry Dash mods.
highlights.detail: It abstracts game internals, providing APIs for level editing, custom objects, and script injection, facilitating community‑driven extensions. The project aims to streamline mod development for both novice and experienced developers.

highlights.title: tensorflow/tensorflow
highlights.summary: TensorFlow is an open source machine learning framework written in C++ for broad use.
highlights.detail: The project provides a comprehensive ecosystem of tools, libraries, and community resources that support model building, training, and deployment across CPUs, GPUs, and specialized accelerators.

items.title: Model: black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein
items.summary: The black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein model has been downloaded 46,123 times and received 460 likes on Hugging Face.
items.detail: It is an image‑to‑image diffusion model that builds on the Flux architecture, targeting fast generation with moderate compute. The popularity indicates strong community interest for creative workflows. The model is released under a permissive license for commercial use.

items.title: Model: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017
items.summary: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, an image‑text‑to‑text model on Hugging Face, has earned 1,110 likes.
items.detail: The model combines visual understanding with language generation, suitable for captioning and visual QA tasks. It is part of DeepSeek's Flash series aimed at low‑latency inference. The repository includes example scripts and a permissive license.

items.title: Model: meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B
items.summary: Meta's Muse‑Spark‑Open‑816B‑A42B model recorded 1,600 downloads and 518 likes on Hugging Face.
items.detail: This 816‑billion‑parameter image‑text model is designed for open‑ended multimodal generation. It demonstrates competitive quality on benchmark datasets while remaining accessible through a hosted inference API. The model is released under an open‑source license for research and commercial use.

items.title: 2026 Retrocomputing Challenge: Dollhouse Arcade Cabinet Runs Remote DOS Games
items.summary: The 2026 Retrocomputing Challenge features a dollhouse‑sized arcade cabinet that streams classic DOS games remotely.
items.detail: Creator Juha Lilja built a miniature cabinet housing a microcontroller that connects to a remote DOS server, delivering video over a small display. The project showcases creative hardware hacking and low‑latency remote gaming, inspiring similar retro‑tech builds.

items.title: 2026 Retrocomputing Challenge: Oldputer Gives Old Eyes Relief with E-ink Display
items.summary: The 2026 Retrocomputing Challenge features the Oldputer, a low‑power computer using an e‑ink display for reduced eye strain.
items.detail: The Oldputer replaces traditional LCD panels with e‑ink, offering high contrast and low refresh rates that are easier on the eyes during long coding sessions. It targets hobbyists interested in vintage hardware aesthetics while providing modern connectivity.

items.title: Building a Flying Drone With a Single Propeller
items.summary: A tutorial demonstrates how to build a functional drone using only a single motor and propeller.
items.detail: The design relies on clever thrust vectoring and lightweight materials to achieve stable flight, but acknowledges that control complexity and payload limits make it impractical for most applications. It serves as a proof‑of‑concept for minimalist UAV engineering.

items.title: Busting the Myth that Plastics are Chemically Inert in Water
items.summary: New experiments show that common plastics can leach chemicals into water, contradicting the claim of inertness.
items.detail: The study measured trace organic compounds released from polyethylene and polypropylene after prolonged immersion, finding measurable concentrations that could affect water quality. Results suggest re‑evaluating plastic use in long‑term water storage.

items.title: Discovering SDRs Everywhere
items.summary: Hackers worldwide are independently creating software‑defined radio (SDR) tools, sparking a rapid expansion of low‑cost radio experimentation.
items.detail: These community‑driven projects repurpose inexpensive hardware like RTL‑SDR dongles, enabling signal decoding, spectrum analysis, and custom protocol development without specialized equipment. The movement mirrors a modern “Precambrian explosion” of open‑source radio innovation.
